title: Fracture severity and biomarker levels in synovial fluid as risk factors for the development of post-traumatic osteoarthritis in tibial plafond fractures
summary:
Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), is a disorder that can develop after joint damage and affects young to middle-aged adults. The risk of developing osteoarthritis after an ankle fracture is very high. 
Although many patients suffer from PTOA, the underlying mechanisms of PTOA development are not well understood. PTOA development appears to be multifactorial and involve complex interactions between various factors. Evidence suggests that both fracture severity and the extent of the inflammatory response in the joint are associated with the development of PTOA. Studies investigating these two aspects simultaneously are lacking. However, since multifactorial development is assumed, it is important to consider multiple factors in order to assess the individual patient's risk of developing PTOA.

The aim of this study is to determine fracture severity in ankle fractures and inflammatory response in ankle fluid and to investigate their potential to predict risk for PTOA development. 

The following hypotheses will be tested: 
1. There is a relationship between the extent of inflammatory reaction in the synovial fluid and the severity of the fracture in patients with acute fractures of the upper ankle. 

2. The extent of fracture severity and increased inflammatory response in synovial fluid in the acute phase after trauma are related to PTOA outcome two years after trauma and thus represent significant risk factors for the development of PTOA.

Patients with acute ankle fractures will be included in this study. The severity of the fracture will be determined by analyzing clinical CT images, and the concentrations of inflammatory markers in the synovial fluid of the fractured ankle will be examined. Two years after treatment of the fracture, a clinical follow-up will determine whether there is functional or radiographic evidence of the development of PTOA through a questionnaire and evaluation of clinical radiographs.
conditions: Fracture of lower end of tibia

interventions.name: Patients with acute tibial plafond fracture will be included in the study. Clinical CT images taken for planning fracture stabilization will be analyzed for the study to determine the severity of the fracture. Synovial fluid will be obtained during the course of surgery for surgical stabilization of

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age: 18 to 60 years 
- Isolated, acute, closed or open AO/OTA 43-B or 43-C fracture as mono-injury 
- Patient is able to understand the study procedure and has given written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy 
- Missing or incomplete clinical CT images 
- Injury to the lower ankle joint  
- Inflammatory arthritis or preexisting osteoarthritis in the injured ankle (previous diagnosis, obvious history, radiographic findings) 
- Other disease of the injured ankle (acute or past) 
- Regular use of non-steroidal or anti-inflammatory drugs 
- Cortisone injection in the injured ankle within 3 months prior to trauma 
- Autoimmune disease 
- Immune suppression
